This app uses FFmpeg to read DV camcorders and capture cards over USB and record the tapes, and to convert unprotected DVDs to MP4: the DV and MJPEG video decoders, the tape audio reader (DV demuxer), the MP4 writer and the MP4 reader (to close an interrupted recording); and, for DVDs, the MPEG-PS reader (the VOB), the MPEG-2 video decoder and the AC-3, MPEG audio (MP2) and DVD LPCM audio decoders. FFmpeg is licensed under the GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1 or later (full text below). Copyright © 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers. FFmpeg is a registered trademark of Fabrice Bellard.

The three libraries ship in the app unmodified, as separate files, dynamically linked (lib/arm64-v8a/libavcodec.so, libavformat.so and libavutil.so). You can replace them with a compatible version you build yourself: FFmpeg 9.0.x for Android arm64, with the same library names (SONAME libavcodec.so, libavformat.so and libavutil.so). The 9.0 series is required because the app uses the DV demuxer interface (avpriv_dv_*), which FFmpeg does not guarantee across versions. To replace them: unpack the APK, replace the files without compression, align (zipalign -P 16 -f 4) and sign (apksigner) with your key, uninstall the original version and install yours.

The exact source code used is the official ffmpeg-%1$s.tar.xz, unmodified (sha256 %2$s), built without GPL components (the configure line is in the build script; in short, --disable-everything --disable-autodetect --enable-decoder=dvvideo --enable-decoder=mjpeg --enable-demuxer=dv --enable-demuxer=mov --enable-muxer=mp4 --enable-demuxer=mpegps --enable-demuxer=mpegvideo --enable-parser=mpegvideo --enable-parser=ac3 --enable-parser=mpegaudio --enable-decoder=mpeg2video --enable-decoder=ac3 --enable-decoder=mp2 --enable-decoder=pcm_dvd --enable-shared). The Quall developer provides this source code and the build script to anyone who asks, for at least three years from the last distribution of this version of the app.
